content.text:
The series Σ (n=1 to ∞) 1/(n³+1) **converges**. Wolfram|Alpha returned "sum_(n=1)^∞ 1/(n^3 + 1) converges" under "Sum convergence," with the infinite sum evaluating to about 0.68650.

I ran the query "sum from n=1 to infinity of 1/(n^3+1)" on wolframalpha.com and read the result pods from the page snapshot. The result also lists a closed form, −(1/3)·Σ polygamma(0, −ω)/(ω²+2ω+1) over the roots ω of ω³+3ω²+3ω+2=0. Wolfram|Alpha displays it as a formula, so I did not evaluate it further.

As an independent check, 1/(n³+1) < 1/n³ for every n, and Σ 1/n³ is a convergent p-series (p = 3 > 1), so the comparison test gives convergence.
